title: Fix tax rounding in order total calculation
executive_summary:
Direct answer: ECR-2026-008 changes Order Service rounding to round tax per currency minor unit after discounts so the authorised amount equals the displayed order total — run the two P0 regression tests TC-1085 and TC-1083 plus the recommended P1s (notably TC-1086, TC-1084 and TC-1089), and add targeted tests for currency-rate precision and service timeouts plus an ISO‑4217 catalogue assertion. 

Why: the change is explicitly intended to fix order-total mismatches and tax-rounding errors (addresses BUG-193 and BUG-410) and the three core tests TC-1085/TC-1083/TC-1089 are already mapped to that fix (tests/top; correlation_findings). 

Risk/gaps to cover: the package shows HIGH risk (score 57) with historical high-severity defects including BUG-188 and BUG-193, and correlation found a design/evidence gap for REQ-1011 and missing coverage for currency-rate precision (BUG-301). 

Actionable additions: add a regression asserting the ISO‑4217 minor‑unit catalogue per CMT-1008, and include explicit tests for BUG-301 (rate precision) and the timeout/recurrence scenarios (BUG-188 / BUG-421).

ecr_overview.title: Fix tax rounding in order total calculation
ecr_overview.description: Correct the order total calculation so tax is rounded per currency minor unit after discounts rather than before, keeping the authorised amount equal to the displayed order total.

change_classification.summary: The order total calculation is being changed to round tax per currency minor unit after applying discounts instead of before, ensuring the authorised payment amount matches the displayed total. This could break payment authorization flows, tax compliance reporting, discount application logic, and any system that relies on the previous rounding sequence.

retrieval_plan.summary: The order total calculation is being changed to round tax per currency minor unit after applying discounts instead of before, ensuring the authorised payment amount matches the displayed total. This could break payment authorization flows, tax compliance reporting, discount application logic, and any system that relies on the previous rounding sequence.
retrieval_plan.dependency_reason: Tax and order total calculations are shared across payment processing, invoicing, reporting, and accounting integrations that depend on consistent rounding behaviour and authorized amount correctness.

correlation_review.summary: The ECR directly addresses BUG-193 (order total mismatch) and BUG-410 (tax rounding) with three P0 tests covering the core fix. However, critical gaps exist: REQ-1011 lacks direct evidence despite being central to the change, and high-risk defects BUG-188 and BUG-421 remain uncovered despite their high recurrence likelihood. A decision concerning currency rejection ordering (REQ-1003, CMT-1003) is well-evidenced but unrelated to the tax rounding fix.

key_links.text: BUG-193 (capture mismatch) is directly addressed by the implementation per CMT-1060 and covered by TC-1085, TC-1083, TC-1089.
BUG-410 (per-line tax rounding) is prevented by three tests explicitly targeting per-currency rounding.
REQ-1003 currency rejection ordering is confirmed by treasury decision and documentary evidence.
BUG-188 and BUG-421 have high recurrence risk but no dedicated tests; current coverage relies on indirect inclusion.

gaps.text: REQ-1011 (core requirement) has test coverage but no explicit evidence document confirming the rounding logic design.
BUG-301 (currency rate precision) remains uncovered by any test despite direct relevance to multi-currency calculations.
REQ-1014, REQ-1015, REQ-1019 are marked relevant but have no recommended tests or coverage evidence.
High-recurrence payment and inventory service timeout defects lack dedicated regression tests in the pack.

defect_summary: ECR-2026-008 affects Order Service where three high-severity defects could happen again: BUG-193 where the order total was recalculated after authorization, BUG-188 where checkout hung due to a missing timeout on the payment service call, and BUG-421 where checkout failed when the inventory service timed out. The team should run tests TC-1085, TC-1083, and TC-1089 to check that order totals match the authorized amount, that payment service delays do not hang the checkout, and that inventory service timeouts do not cause checkout failures. Additionally, BUG-309 could happen again in the frontend portal with a medium chance, so the team should run TC-1082, TC-1081, and TC-1079 to verify that the checkout button cannot be double-submitted.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.body:
Direct answer: ECR-2026-008 changes Order Service rounding to round tax per currency minor unit after discounts so the authorised amount equals the displayed order total — run the two P0 regression tests TC-1085 and TC-1083 plus the recommended P1s (notably TC-1086, TC-1084 and TC-1089), and add targeted tests for currency-rate precision and service timeouts plus an ISO‑4217 catalogue assertion. 

Why: the change is explicitly intended to fix order-total mismatches and tax-rounding errors (addresses BUG-193 and BUG-410) and the three core tests TC-1085/TC-1083/TC-1089 are already mapped to that fix (tests/top; correlation_findings). 

Risk/gaps to cover: the package shows HIGH risk (score 57) with historical high-severity defects including BUG-188 and BUG-193, and correlation found a design/evidence gap for REQ-1011 and missing coverage for currency-rate precision (BUG-301). 

Actionable additions: add a regression asserting the ISO‑4217 minor‑unit catalogue per CMT-1008, and include explicit tests for BUG-301 (rate precision) and the timeout/recurrence scenarios (BUG-188 / BUG-421).

sections.title: Defect Analysis
sections.body: ECR-2026-008 affects Order Service where three high-severity defects could happen again: BUG-193 where the order total was recalculated after authorization, BUG-188 where checkout hung due to a missing timeout on the payment service call, and BUG-421 where checkout failed when the inventory service timed out. The team should run tests TC-1085, TC-1083, and TC-1089 to check that order totals match the authorized amount, that payment service delays do not hang the checkout, and that inventory service timeouts do not cause checkout failures. Additionally, BUG-309 could happen again in the frontend portal with a medium chance, so the team should run TC-1082, TC-1081, and TC-1079 to verify that the checkout button cannot be double-submitted.

sections.title: Correlation Findings
sections.body:
The ECR directly addresses BUG-193 (order total mismatch) and BUG-410 (tax rounding) with three P0 tests covering the core fix. However, critical gaps exist: REQ-1011 lacks direct evidence despite being central to the change, and high-risk defects BUG-188 and BUG-421 remain uncovered despite their high recurrence likelihood. A decision concerning currency rejection ordering (REQ-1003, CMT-1003) is well-evidenced but unrelated to the tax rounding fix.
- Gap: REQ-1011 (core requirement) has test coverage but no explicit evidence document confirming the rounding logic design.
- Gap: BUG-301 (currency rate precision) remains uncovered by any test despite direct relevance to multi-currency calculations.
- Gap: REQ-1014, REQ-1015, REQ-1019 are marked relevant but have no recommended tests or coverage evidence.
- Gap: High-recurrence payment and inventory service timeout defects lack dedicated regression tests in the pack.
- Key link: BUG-193 (capture mismatch) is directly addressed by the implementation per CMT-1060 and covered by TC-1085, TC-1083, TC-1089.
- Key link: BUG-410 (per-line tax rounding) is prevented by three tests explicitly targeting per-currency rounding.
- Key link: REQ-1003 currency rejection ordering is confirmed by treasury decision and documentary evidence.
